correctness.rationale: PASS: In squared-radius variable u with v=1-u, the disk and outer-annulus radial Gram matrices are G_ij=B(m+1,i+j+1), B_ij(eps)=int_0^eps v^(i+j)(1-v)^m dv, and their generalized eigenvalues are concentration eigenvalues (common pi cancels). Since B(eps)/eps tends to e_0e_0^T, lambda_max/eps tends to (G^-1)00=(n+1)(n+m+1), the Jacobi endpoint Christoffel kernel. Write B=D_eps(H+O(eps))D_eps, D_jj=eps^(j+1/2), H_ij=1/(i+j+1). Then eps^(2n+1) B^-1G tends to (H^-1)nn e_ne_n^T G, whose only positive eigenvalue is (2n+1)binom(2n,n)^2 B(m+1,2n+1); reciprocation gives sharp lambda_min and spectral condition number. At n=1, m->infinity with eps=tau/(m+1), the measure tends to exp(-x)dx, so the two eigenvalues of its 2x2 [1,1-x] restricted moment Gram matrix are Lambda_+/-=1-e^-tau(1+tau^2/2) +/- tau e^-tau sqrt(1+tau^2/4). Positive mass on both sides gives 0<Lambda_-<Lambda_+<1. Independent high-precision beta-moment generalized eigenvalues at three (m,n) pairs and two thicknesses matched leading constants; finite checks corroborate but do not prove fixed-n or m-growing limits.
